description.value: A functional MRI study examining brain responses to guided stress and neutral imagery in cocaine-dependent individuals and healthy controls, including between-group differences and associations between BOLD activity and cocaine craving.

value: we hypothesized that brain responses to stress would differ between cocaine abusers and healthy controls.
We also predicted that neural activity during stress-induced cocaine craving would involve frontal–limbic–striatal circuitry associated with both emotion and reward processing.

value: Patients showed increased bilateral activation in the dorsal striatum and caudate region during stress, as well as significant activation in the thalamus/putamen, posterior cingulate, and superior frontal gyrus; they also showed significant deactivation in the medial orbitofrontal/anterior cingulate region. The increased dorsal striatal/caudate activity may represent the automatized, well-learned, habit-based nature of craving and drug-use behaviors in addiction.

value: During stress, controls showed significantly greater activation than cocaine-dependent individuals in the anterior cingulate, left hippocampal/parahippocampal gyrus, and right fusiform gyrus. Patients showed deactivation in the right postcentral gyrus, whereas controls showed increased anterior cingulate activity and patients showed decreased activity. This pattern suggests decreased emotion regulation and cognitive control in patients.

value: In patients, cocaine craving was significantly associated with activity in the right caudate and right dorsomedial thalamus/striatal region. Right dorsolateral prefrontal and left posterior insula/superior temporal activity also correlated positively with cocaine craving. The stress-induced cocaine-craving-related dorsal striatum/caudate activity may represent the automatized, habit-based nature of craving and drug-use behaviors in addiction.

name.value: guided imagery and recall of stress and neutral situations

spans.text: Blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) signal changes were assessed in a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) session with healthy controls and treatment-engaged, abstinent, cocaine-dependent individuals (patients) as they participated in brief guided imagery and recall of three personal stress and three personal neutral situations.

description.value: Participants listened to personalized stress and neutral scripts during guided imagery and verbally rated distress, craving, and imagery vividness.

spans.text: Patients were also asked to rate their desire for cocaine (cocaine craving) on an auditory analog Likert scale ranging from 0–10.
Three stress imagery scripts were developed for each subject.

description.value: Three personalized stressful situations rated at least 8 on a 10-point distress scale were presented through 2-minute guided imagery and recall, followed by 30 seconds of quiet imagery; each trial also included baseline and post-imagery recovery periods.

spans.text: Only situations rated as 8 or above on this scale were accepted as appropriate for script development.
In addition to the stress scripts, three neutral-relaxing scripts were also developed from personalized, neutral, drug-free situations.

description.value: Three personalized neutral, drug-free relaxing situations were presented through 2-minute guided imagery and recall, followed by 30 seconds of quiet imagery; each trial also included baseline and post-imagery recovery periods.
